svg.text: "Should I use a HELOC or a cash-out refi?"
Same model. Same question. Only difference: one line in the system prompt.

g.text: Great question! This is a really common dilemma and
honestly, there's no one-size-fits-all answer. It kind of
depends on your situation, your goals, and your comfort
level with risk. Some people find that a HELOC gives them
more flexibility, while others prefer the predictability of a
refi. You might want to think about how long you plan to
stay in the home, and it could be worth running the
numbers with a professional. That said, if I had to lean
one way, I'd probably say a HELOC might make sense if
you don't need all the money at once, but again, it really
comes down to what feels right for you. Hope this helps,
and feel free to ask if you have any other questions!
✗ filler ✗ idioms ✗ hedging ✗ hint instead of instruction ✗ no numbers
I'm assuming you want cash for one project under
$100k and your current mortgage rate is below 5%.
If so: HELOC.
Reason: a refi replaces your whole mortgage at today's
rate. A HELOC only charges interest on what you draw.
Required before deciding: your current rate, loan balance,
and the amount you need. Tell me those 3 numbers and
I will show the 10-year cost of each option.
One question: what is your current mortgage rate?
✓ answer first ✓ assumption stated ✓ required labeled ✓ one question ✓ no filler
